inapplicable.reason: T01 starts no task, actor, stream or session. Its cases are synchronous reads of pinned files and judged logs, and the X02 probe is a one-shot guest process, so there is no durable operation to cancel. The one thing that can run long, a hung probe, is cut by a single absolute deadline and tested (bounded-and-confined).

No state survives between runs: a run reads files, writes a new exclusive receipt and exits, and a rerun is a new run that keeps the old receipt (rerun-keeps-original). There is no process to restart, resume or recover. The guest's own reboot belongs to the E07 supervisor envelope, which the X02 judge requires as a transcript fact.

No test input is random and no clock decides a verdict. Expected outcomes are hand-written tables and exhaustive itertools.product grids, and the probe's known-answer vectors are fixed. The clock and random uses are recorded or bounding only: the receipt's finished time, the diagnostic log's monotonic timebase, the absolute probe deadline (a bound, not an input) and a random run id (an identifier). The probe's one draw from the operating system's random source is a capability check whose phase result is judged, not a seeded test input. So there is no seed to publish.

inapplicable.criterion: Render path emits bounded counters/events to a nonblocking sink; verify slow/full/unavailable log sinks do not change audio deadlines.
inapplicable.reason: T01 has no render path, no audio and no deadline. The analogous property, that a slow, full or unavailable diagnostic sink cannot change a case verdict, holds in the shared Q00 sink (tests/t01/case_log.py never blocks or raises) and lost evidence only marks a run not qualified (evidence-loss-is-incomplete). Audio-deadline checks belong to the render-path packages.

inapplicable.criterion: pseudonymous member/group IDs, source epoch, command/state revision, queue/latency/resource counters, injected fault schedule and causal error chain
inapplicable.reason: T01 has no members, groups, sources or commands, so there is no id, epoch or revision to log. The counters it has are the diagnostic log's events/critical/dropped counts and the X02 probe's resource readings; a failure's first cause is named by exception type in the case detail; planted faults are named in each test, not scheduled over time.

independent_anchors.note: figures obtained with a different tool from the probes (a shell grep over the supplied source), so a probe regression is not checked against itself

x01_build.note: The pins of the compile-only gate T01-X01, written by hand from the resolved consumer workspace and the first real PowerPC log, not produced by the judge. consumer_files are the sha256 of the four files a cargo run in the consumer reads (the lock is the cargo-resolved 183-package lock of mail 10200); lock_packages and lock_registry come from the shell commands below (lock_path is their difference), so the judge's own lock parse is checked against another tool. The std fingerprint is the compiler_builtins version in the nightly-2026-08-31 library source that the first real log compiled, and std_registry are the seven crates.io crates that build-std itself compiles (all seven are in library/Cargo.lock of that toolchain's rust-src, which was read separately); any other registry crate must be in the consumer lock. The contract asks for two attempts per target, the seven core crates (core: -p x01_core in the consumer workspace) and the whole library (whole: -p tailscale in the pinned tailscale-rs workspace); `attempts` names each one's manifest and package. Nothing here is a runtime, memory, CPU or enrollment figure.

cc_wrappers.note: The C compiler for aws-lc-sys on the whole-library MIPS attempt. cargo's own env table sets CC_mips_unknown_linux_musl through exactly three explicit --config keys (value, relative, force) naming one of the three wrapper files below, which root syncs beside the tree under x01-cc/. All enforce Zig 0.14.1 and Zig's big-endian o32 soft-float target (mips-linux-musleabi). The first is a byte copy of toolchain/linker/zig-cc-mips-be and passes cc-rs's Rust --target spelling through, which Zig rejects; the second drops exactly the two known --target spellings and refuses --target=OTHER and -target, but forwarded the bare two-argument --target OTHER and -target=OTHER; the third (v2) refuses all of those overrides, and is the one to ship. The one-key inline-table spelling is refused by cargo and is accepted only as a record of that refusal. No other --config argument and no other file under x01-cc/ is accepted.
